semantically_equivalent_models.justification: Matrix factorization encompasses techniques like singular value decomposition (SVD), which is used to factorize a matrix into components. Therefore, 'matrix factorization' can be considered semantically equivalent to singular value decomposition as SVD is one of the well-known methods under matrix factorization.

parent_models.justification: Singular value decomposition is a specific technique within the broader area of matrix factorization, hence 'matrix factorization' is a parent model to SVD.

closest_parent_model.justification: As singular value decomposition is a specific type of matrix factorization, 'matrix factorization' is the closest and only parent model in the context of the provided list.

child_models.justification: Nonnegative matrix factorization is a specific type of matrix factorization where the factors are nonnegative. While it's distinct from traditional singular value decomposition, both are types of matrix factorization.

closest_child_model.justification: Within the realm of matrix factorization, nonnegative matrix factorization is the closest child model listed, as it shares the same foundational principle of factorizing a matrix.

closest_sibling_model.justification: There are no sibling models in this context because singular value decomposition is quite distinct, and the list does not include other models that fall under 'matrix factorization' without being more specific like nonnegative matrix factorization.

unrelated_models.justification: Linear discriminant analysis is unrelated to singular value decomposition as it is a classification technique rather than a matrix factorization method.
